name: clone
synopsis: int clone(int (*fn)(void *), void *stack, int flags, void *arg, ...);
long syscall(SYS_clone3, struct clone_args *cl_args, size_t size);
description: The clone system call creates a new child process similar to fork(2), but allows more precise control over shared execution contexts such as memory, file descriptors, and namespaces. The child process can execute a specified function with an argument, and various flags determine what resources are shared.

parameters.name: fn
parameters.description: Function pointer to the function executed by the child process

parameters.name: stack
parameters.description: Pointer to the stack for the child process

parameters.name: flags
parameters.description: Bit mask of flags to control shared resources and behavior

parameters.name: arg
parameters.description: Argument passed to the function fn

parameters.name: parent_tid
parameters.description: Optional: Pointer to store the child's TID in the parent's memory

parameters.name: tls
parameters.description: Optional: Location of the new thread-local storage

parameters.name: child_tid
parameters.description: Optional: Pointer to store the child's TID in the child's memory

return_value.success: Returns the thread ID of the child process
return_value.failure: Returns -1 and sets errno to indicate the error

errors.description: CLONE_INTO_CGROUP was specified but restrictions not met (clone3() only)
Too many processes are already running
CLONE_INTO_CGROUP specified but cgroup has a domain controller enabled (clone3() only)
One or more PIDs in set_tid already exist (clone3() only)
Insufficient memory to create the child process

bugs: The CLONE_DETACHED flag has no effect and is ignored in modern kernels; some flag combinations may lead to unexpected behavior as noted in the man page.
versions: Linux 2.0 and later, with extensions like clone3() in Linux 5.3
